reply.summary: Rewrote docs/designs/tasks/001-steam-linux-discovery/01-research.md for T-001 (Linux Steam discovery plugin), re-verifying the repo seam first-hand — the two-method DiscoveryPlugin trait, five-field DiscoveredGame with Platform::SteamLinux, normalize_slug, the error-swallowing DiscoveryEngine, DummyPlugin-only CLI, the 32-package Cargo.lock with no VDF parser or tempfile, and the CLI test that asserts `[]` — and re-fetching every external citation this run. Format evidence is consistent: ACF text KeyValues rooted at AppState carrying appid/name/StateFlags/installdir, composition rule <library>/steamapps/common/<installdir>, and StateFlags bit 4 = StateFullyInstalled per the Lutris table. New evidence added over the prior pass: three current Rust scanners (fragcap-steam, steamie-core, yandere-core) that hand-roll a small KeyValues reader instead of taking keyvalues-parser+pest, the pre-2021 vs modern libraryfolders.vdf shapes that already caused a silent-zero-libraries bug, per-game Proton prefix directories holding look-alike libraryfolders.vdf copies, and divergent backslash-escape handling across implementations. Lenses applied: prior art, platform notes (root candidate list, Flatpak sandbox visibility, arbitrary mounts, Rust 1.85/edition-2024 and --locked gate), and security landscape under Risks & unknowns (install_path as a privilege hand-off, whole-scan blast radius, diagnostic leakage). The designer's decisions are enumerated as 19 open questions: root policy, test seam and fixtures, dependency posture, grammar subset and escaping, non-game filtering, StateFlags and missing-name handling, path validation, per-file failure policy, ordering/dedup, error taxonomy, and performance budget.
